When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **3/10** (WARNING, price action still orderly) vs VIX Spike Tier **4/4** (EXTREME, **85%** spike probability)
Price has not broken, but options are pricing a vol expansion, with skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger all active. Trust the VIX tier for timing risk, since options reprice before prices do. Trust the Crash Index only for how much damage has already happened, which is little.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime state **73** (topping watch, action zone) vs Contrarian score **44** (ACCUMULATE, partial signal)
One reading says distribute into strength, the other says start buying weakness. The contrarian score is only partial at **44**, while the regime score and the divergence composite both point to topping. Trust the topping read for sizing, and treat the accumulate signal as an early watchlist flag.
Today's tension
The options market prices a volatility spike at **4/4**, yet credit, small caps and the yen have not confirmed it.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at only **3/10**, none of the **3** confluence checks is active, and the Nasdaq 100 is up **+2.5%** over five days. The contrarian score of **44** says dip buyers still get a partial signal to accumulate.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector reads **EXTREME** with an **85%** spike probability, and **67.4%** of **43** tracked pairs are diverging, **26** of them bearish against **3** bullish. The regime score of **73** sits in the action zone with a topping bias.
The tell: Watch whether credit stress (HYG), a small cap drawdown or yen safe haven flow switches on alongside VIX backwardation. One of the three lighting up turns the options warning into a confirmed signal.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

Concentration is the call. The Nasdaq 100 leads at +2.5% over five days while the Russell 2000 sits at -0.1%, and the regime model reads CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence. The regime score of 73 puts you in the action zone with a topping bias: 2 concentration signals against 1 risk-on signal. Index level looks fine. Underneath, a few large stocks are carrying it.

Positioning follows from that. The VIX Spike Detector is at 4/4 with 85% spike probability, and the Crash Index is only 3/10. That gap says protection is cheap relative to what options traders now expect, and it's the time to hold hedges rather than build new risk. Trim the extended leaders, keep some cash, and let the contrarian score of 44 tell you where to start buying if weakness arrives. It's a partial signal, so it earns a small starter and nothing more.

The main risk is a sharp unwind in the leaders while 67.4% of pairs are already diverging. The flip signal is confirmation from outside the VIX: credit stress, a small cap drawdown or yen strength. None of those fire today, with 0 confluences active. If one does, treat the topping watch as a live top. If the VIX tier drops while the Russell 2000 turns positive, the concentration read loses its edge.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift is how far that relationship has shifted between an earlier window and the recent one.

Today the composite zone is TOPPING, with 67.4% of 43 pairs diverging, 26 bearish and 3 bullish, for a net bias of 23. The jaws score is 100, the maximum.

The sharpest breaks all score 80. Nasdaq 100 versus S&P 500 went from +0.88 to -0.17, so tech no longer tracks the index it sits inside.

Regional banks versus financials went from +0.24 to -0.70, which flags stress in smaller lenders. Visa versus Mastercard went from +0.79 to -0.67, and AUD/JPY went from +0.41 to -0.21, a risk appetite gauge losing its link.

Nvidia versus AMD flipped from -0.83 to +0.31. Min vol versus S&P 500 moved from -0.94 to -0.08.

Relationships that held for months are breaking together, and that pattern tends to show up near turns. Treat it as a reason to cut crowded leaders, and wait for credit or small caps before calling a top.

Leadership is uneven across the globe. In Asia, the Nikkei is up +7.9% over five days while Shanghai is down -2.8%, so Japan is carrying the region alone.

Europe is split between the DAX at +0.2% and the CAC 40 at -2.1%. In the US, the Nasdaq 100 leads at +2.5% and the Russell 2000 lags at -0.1%.

Crypto trades around the clock and gave the weakest read, with Bitcoin at -1.5% and Ether at -3.6%. Ether trailing Bitcoin is a sign that the riskiest buyers are stepping back.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The two gauges disagree, and that's a coherent state. The Crash Index at 3/10 measures damage already visible in prices, and so far the damage is small.

The VIX Spike Detector at 4/4 measures what options traders are paying for protection, and it reads EXTREME with 85% spike probability. Skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger are all active at once.

Backwardation means near term volatility costs more than later volatility, which is how the market prices a shock it expects soon. Price calm with options fear usually means big money is hedging before it sells.

You should respect the VIX reading for timing, since it moves first. The Crash Index would need to climb well above 3/10 before the damage is real.

Until then, stay hedged and don't add leverage.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
